sectionGuide.why: Benchmarks, scenarios, traces, and participants describe *how* measurement runs — distinct from properties of the agent. Benchmark inventories live in this vocabulary; treating a benchmark name as a dimension breaks gap analysis.
sectionGuide.wgUse: Benchmark landscape and coverage inventories. Benchmark vs leaderboard distinction. Each inventory row uses these nouns for harness, user, infrastructure, and tool participants. Less blocking for core property sign-off — review when inventory schema is agreed.
sectionGuide.enables: Benchmark landscape and external coverage matrices; evaluation envelopes; clean separation of agent properties from harness and dataset furniture.
sectionGuide.priorities: **P1** = core ecosystem nouns every inventory row needs (benchmark, scenario, trace, tool). **P2** = secondary participants (evaluator, message bus). Can track inventory schema as it matures.

categories.relevance: Names harness participants and artefacts (benchmark, scenario, trace, tool, user, infrastructure) — evaluation scope must declare which rings are in scope.
categories.wgUse: Benchmark landscape · external coverage spreadsheets · not agent properties

terms.definition: A published or organisation-standard collection of evaluation scenarios, scoring rules, and reporting conventions used to compare systems on accuracy or reliability dimensions.
terms.scopeNote: Statistical coverage assesses how well a benchmark represents production tasks. Distinct from a leaderboard, which may publish only best-of-k or single-run scores.
terms.literatureNote: Inventory and coverage analysis in gap analysis (see running notes matrix). AAIF term for the evaluation artefact, not a quality dimension.

terms.definition: The information available to an agent when making a decision — including user messages, tool results, retrieved documents, memory, and system instructions assembled for the current step.
terms.scopeNote: Incomplete or wrong context is a common root cause of reasoning failure; distinct from the context sources it is built from.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The process by which an agent or runtime selects, orders, trims, and formats material from context sources into the working context for a decision step.
terms.scopeNote: Errors here are agent-side even when individual sources are correct.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: Any origin from which context is drawn: user input, tool output, retrieval hit, memory record, or another agent's message.
terms.scopeNote: Evaluation should record which sources contributed to a decision for attribution and grounding checks.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The interface where an external request, message, or event first enters an agent or multi-agent system — for example an API route, queue consumer, or orchestrator trigger. Defines the outer boundary for traceability and infrastructure failure attribution.
terms.scopeNote: Errors before the entry point are infrastructure; errors after are candidates for agent or coordination attribution.
terms.literatureNote: Operational concept from distributed systems; needed so evaluation scenarios declare where measurement begins.

terms.definition: A person or system role involved in requesting, operating, evaluating, or governing an agentic system. Participant type determines which signals and success criteria apply.
terms.scopeNote: Separates user-perceived reliability from operator and evaluator views in charter validation.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: A single task instance within an evaluation — including inputs, environment setup, perturbations, and expected results. The atomic unit of an evaluation run.
terms.scopeNote: Reliability evaluation repeats the same scenario; robustness evaluation varies it. Scenarios may belong to a benchmark or stand alone.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The runtime environment, orchestration services, tools, APIs, data services, and message paths that surround an agent and deliver inputs and outputs at the agent boundary. As an entity, infrastructure is what infrastructure reliability and infrastructure failure refer to.
terms.scopeNote: Not the agent itself. Health of infrastructure must be established before attributing failures to agent reasoning.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: A ranked comparison surface that publishes scores from one or more evaluation runs — often emphasising a single best attempt (pass@1 or best-of-k) rather than a full benchmark protocol, repeat-run reliability, or a declared evaluation envelope.
terms.scopeNote: Not interchangeable with Benchmark. Leaderboard rank alone does not establish workflow-level, user-ring, or governance-qualified claims.
terms.literatureNote: Common in NLP and agent marketing (MMLU, HELM tables). gap analysis flags procurement risk when leaderboard scores stand in for deployment guarantees.

terms.definition: The configured path, credentials, and routing rules an agent runtime uses to invoke language or multimodal models — including provider APIs, private endpoints, and fallback models.
terms.scopeNote: Model access failures are infrastructure failures until proven otherwise. Access configuration is part of reproducible agent specification.
terms.literatureNote: Vendor-neutral term for deployment slides that name specific provider APIs. Provider names belong in academicTerms or scenario metadata only.

terms.definition: A person responsible for running, monitoring, or approving agentic systems in production — including escalation, policy gates, and incident response.
terms.scopeNote: Receives observability signals and correction escalations; distinct from the end user.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: A service that routes tasks among agents, manages workflow state, and coordinates handoffs in a multi-agent system or pipeline.
terms.scopeNote: Failures may originate in orchestration topology rather than in a single agent.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The software environment that loads agent specifications, executes decision loops, invokes tools, enforces policy hooks, and emits telemetry.
terms.scopeNote: ARWG defines required behaviour at this boundary; specific products are out of scope.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: Measurements and events emitted during execution — latency, errors, tool calls, retries, resource use, and structured logs — used to assess infrastructure health and support failure attribution.
terms.scopeNote: ARWG defines what telemetry categories matter for accuracy and reliability; emission standards belong to Observability WG.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The configured destination where runtime telemetry, traces, and audit logs are emitted — files, collectors, or observability backends. Required so accuracy and reliability claims can be verified post hoc.
terms.scopeNote: ARWG defines what signals must reach the telemetry path; Observability WG defines formats and pipelines.
terms.literatureNote: Infrastructure term from deployment architecture; links specification properties to audit requirements.

terms.definition: An external function, API, or service an agent may call to retrieve data or perform an action. Tool results are primary context sources and evidence inputs.
terms.scopeNote: Tool availability and result quality are common infrastructure failure points.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The set of tools an agent is allowed to invoke, including authentication, network paths, and schema bindings declared in the agent specification.
terms.scopeNote: Tool access misconfiguration causes authorization failures and fabricated tool results. Must be pinned for evaluation reproducibility.
terms.literatureNote: Standard in agent harness design; AAIF separates access (infrastructure) from tool result quality (world layer).

terms.definition: A time-ordered record of steps taken during a task — model calls, tool invocations, messages, policy decisions, and outcomes — used for trajectory analysis and audit.
terms.scopeNote: Conceptual counterpart to trajectory; trace is the recorded artifact, trajectory is the path taken.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.

terms.definition: The person or client system that submits a task, receives outputs, and judges whether the agent met their intent. User behaviour — re-prompts, overrides, abandonment — is a first-class reliability input.
terms.scopeNote: Distinct from operator and evaluator roles.
terms.literatureNote: Harness and participant vocabulary for gap analysis inventory. Describes how measurement runs, not agent properties.
